Section 1: Pointers and Memory Addresses.
In C++, a pointer holds the memory address of an object. The dereference operator allows accessing the value stored at that address. Pointers are foundational for dynamic data structures.

Section 2: AVL Tree Balancing and Rotations.
An AVL tree is a self-balancing binary search tree. When an insertion causes an imbalance factor exceeding plus or minus one, single or double rotations (left-rotation, right-rotation) are performed to restore O(log n) search height.

Section 3: Graph Traversals and Shortest Paths.
Dijkstra algorithm finds the shortest path between nodes in a graph with non-negative edge weights. It uses a priority queue to greedily explore the closest unvisited vertices.
An AVL Tree performs left and right rotations to maintain log(n) height.
